biological.citation: Piazza et al. 2018 - SETBP1 induces transcription of a network of development genes by acting as an epigenetic hub (PMID: 29875417)
biological.summary: SETBP1 binds genomic DNA at AT-rich promoter regions through its AT-hooks and activates transcription by recruiting a HCF1/KMT2A/PHF8 epigenetic complex. Targets such as MECOM are upregulated in SETBP1-mutant leukemias, and deleting two AT-hooks abolishes binding and target upregulation. The targets are enriched for visceral organ development and brain morphogenesis genes. In utero electroporation of mutant SETBP1 impairs mouse neurogenesis and delays neuronal migration.

biological.citation: Banfi et al. 2021 - SETBP1 accumulation induces P53 inhibition and genotoxic stress in neural progenitors underlying neurodegeneration in Schinzel-Giedion syndrome (PMID: 34193871)
biological.summary: In a human SGS neural progenitor model, SETBP1 accumulation stabilizes SET, which blocks P53 acetylation and inhibits P53 function. This causes aberrant proliferation, unresolved DNA damage and apoptosis resistance. The resulting neurodegeneration was alleviated by PARP-1 inhibition or NAD+ supplementation.

biological.citation: Makishima/Sakaguchi et al. 2013 - Somatic SETBP1 mutations in myeloid malignancies (PMID: 23832012)
biological.summary: Recurrent somatic SETBP1 mutations at Asp868, Ser869, Gly870, Ile871 and Asp880 match SGS germline mutations. They were found in 17% of secondary AML and 15% of CMML cases and appear to be gain-of-function. Mutant Setbp1 immortalized mouse myeloid progenitors with greater proliferative capacity than wild-type Setbp1. Mutations were associated with monosomy 7/del(7q) and poor prognosis.

biological.citation: ASHG 2016 - Genetic and functional comparison of identical germline and somatic SETBP1 mutations
biological.summary: Overexpression experiments show that hotspot mutations destroy the SETBP1 degron and increase protein levels, with varying effects on stability. Saturation genome editing of the hotspot and surrounding region showed that mutations common in leukemia disrupt the degron more strongly than those common in SGS. This supports a genotype-phenotype correlation across molecular, cellular and clinical phenotypes.

biological.citation: Review 2017 - Somatic SETBP1 mutations in myeloid neoplasms (PMID: 28447248)
biological.summary: SETBP1 regulates self-renewal through HOXA-protein activation. Mutant SETBP1 attenuates RUNX1 and activates MYB. Mouse models support its role in myeloid leukemogenesis, particularly together with ASXL1 mutations.

biological.citation: 2024 - SETBP1 activation upon MDM4-enhanced ubiquitination of NR3C1 triggers dissemination of colorectal cancer cells (PMID: 38796806)
biological.summary: NR3C1 (glucocorticoid receptor) represses SETBP1 transcription by binding its promoter. MDM4 ubiquitinates NR3C1 and drives its proteasomal degradation, which derepresses SETBP1. SETBP1 knockdown reduced migration, invasion and EMT of CRC cells, and reduced metastasis in mouse xenografts.

biological.citation: 2022 - Genome-Wide Analysis of Disordered Eating Behavior in the Mexican Population (PMID: 35057575)
biological.summary: Summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) analysis linked DNA methylation levels at SETBP1 to disordered eating behavior.

biological.citation: 2025 - Machine Learning-Based Predictive Modeling Maximizes the Efficacy of mTOR/p53 Co-Targeting Therapy Against AML (PMID: 40785506)
biological.summary: Mouse AML cells carrying SETBP1/ASXL1 mutations were resistant to rapamycin, unlike MLL-AF9 AML cells, which were highly sensitive.

biological.citation: Schinzel-Giedion syndrome case report 2024 - Novel SETBP1 D874V adjacent to the degron causes canonical Schinzel-Giedion syndrome (PMID: 38711130)
biological.summary: A novel D874V missense variant adjacent to the degron (aa868-871) caused canonical SGS. This is the first non-degron missense variant reported to do so, consistent with gain-of-function and extending the genotype-phenotype spectrum.

biological.citation: Hamdan et al. 2014 - De novo mutations in moderate or severe intellectual disability (PMID: 25356899)
biological.summary: A likely pathogenic de novo SETBP1 mutation was identified among known ID genes in an exome trio study. Network analysis placed SETBP1 and SET (also found mutated) among interacting ID-associated gene products.
